accepted_fact_texts: Pigs have amazing snouts packed with thousands of smell receptors! Their sense of smell is one of the best in the whole animal world.
Pigs are some of the smartest animals and can even recognize individual faces and sounds. They love rolling in mud—not because they're dirty, but to stay cool on hot days!

attempts.fact_text: Pigs are super smart animals that can recognize themselves in mirrors! Their snouts have an amazing sense of smell so powerful they can find truffles buried deep underground.
attempts.source_note: Wikipedia article on Pig — verified facts about pig intelligence (mirror self-recognition), physical features (snout structure), and olfactory abilities (truffle detection).

problems: Plausibility/sourcing: the mirror claim overstates the science. Published work (Broadbent & Held, 2009) shows pigs can use a mirror to locate food they can see reflected — mirror-guided problem solving, not mirror self-recognition. Pigs have not passed the mark test, so 'recognize themselves in mirrors' is not source-grounded and should be reworded to something like using a mirror to find a snack.
Minor accuracy stretch: truffles grow a few inches to roughly a foot below the surface, so 'buried deep underground' overstates it; 'buried under the soil' would be truer and just as fun.

attempts.fact_text: Pigs have amazing snouts packed with thousands of smell receptors! Their sense of smell is one of the best in the whole animal world.
attempts.source_note: kids.nationalgeographic.com (National Geographic Kids pig article) and en.wikipedia.org (Pig Wikipedia article) confirm pigs possess over 1,100 genes for smell receptors, enabling exceptional olfactory abilities.
